title: Growing to a 13-piece band, Nick Cooper's writing
summary: After the fire the band grew from seven or eight to thirteen pieces, with Nick Cooper writing impressive arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, how did the band go? Eventually it became a big band.
Yeah, well, eventually as the club -- the club was large.

After the first one burned down, the place. So then I started over there with about seven pieces or eight pieces. And then I continued to — Mike, talk to him. So we went up to about 13 pieces. That's the time when Buddy was talking about, that he would come over, and then it was just a 13-piece band and these chorus -- well, there was a lot of excitement, man. And then we had special arrangements. I had a boy writing for me at that time, who later died of cancer, Nick Cooper. And he was a tremendous writer. And he did some things for one of the screen things in -- which was unheard-of then. But these local arrangers and things for -- what was his name, Tompkin?
Yeah, right, and so he did some things -- he was a great musician. This was when the Schillinger method first started.
And he was writing, and his arrange-
ments were just fabulous. Then we had Lurlene Hunter there one time, singing.
